english.title: Give false / misleading name / address / information re s.5(9) requirement - Control of Pollution
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being an occupant of a vehicle, namely **(..SPECIFY VEHICLE MAKE AND INDEX NUMBER..), in response to a requirement made under section 5(9) of the Control of Pollution (Amendment) Act 1989 by

(A)_[an authorised officer of a regulation authority, namely **(..SPECIFY THE AUTHORITY..),]_
(B)_[a constable]_

to provide

(C)_[your name and address,]_
(D)_[the name and address of the registered owner of the vehicle,]_
(E)_[information, namely **(..SPECIFY..), which that officer had reasonably requested,]_
(F)_[**(..SPECIFY WHERE THE FAILURE INVOLVES MORE THAN ONE OF THE ABOVE OPTIONS..),]_

gave information

(G)_[knowing it to be]_
(H)_[recklessly which was]_

false or misleading in a material way, namely **(..SPECIFY..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section 5(10)(b) and (11) of the Control of Pollution (Amendment) Act 1989.

english.notes: This offence was inserted by section 37 of the Clean Neighbourhoods and Environment Act 2005.

other.penalty:
A fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Time limit on prosecutions
6 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
